name: Pantoprazole
route_note: Oral delayed-release tablets or granules once daily; IV injection or infusion
originator: Byk Gulden (Konstanz, Germany), with Smith Kline & French

discovery.note: A difluoromethoxy benzimidazole PPI designed for greater chemical stability at near-neutral pH.

tagline: Proton pump inhibitor with an IV form and fewer CYP interactions
summary: Pantoprazole is a proton pump inhibitor used orally and intravenously to suppress gastric acid. Compared with omeprazole it has a lower potential for CYP-mediated drug interactions and is widely used in hospitals for stress-ulcer prophylaxis and upper GI bleeding.
mechanism: Pantoprazole is activated in the acid environment of parietal cells to a cyclic sulfenamide, which binds covalently to cysteine residues (including Cys813 and Cys822) on the H+/K+ ATPase.
Its greater stability at mildly acidic pH means activation is more confined to the parietal cell, and acid secretion resumes only as new pumps are made.
uses: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and erosive oesophagitis
Upper gastrointestinal bleeding and stress-ulcer prophylaxis (IV)

history.title: IV formulation
history.detail: FDA approves Protonix IV, the first IV PPI in the US.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic pantoprazole enters the US market after at-risk launches and patent litigation.

history.title: Patent settlement
history.detail: Teva and Sun agree to pay Pfizer and Takeda $2.15 billion over at-risk generic launches.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP2C19 demethylation followed by sulfation; minor CYP3A4

facts: Pantoprazole was the first PPI available as an intravenous formulation in the US.
Pantoprazole can cause false-positive urine screening tests for THC.
